paragraphs: This is an occupation requiring long medical education, clinical training, practice registration, and organizational surgical authorization; observation or simulation exercises cannot be treated as qualifications to operate.

The core work is integrating history, physical examination, imaging, and other tests to judge whether surgery is necessary, discussing risks and non-surgical options with the patient, and then performing compliant surgery.

Suited to those willing to continuously take on high-risk clinical judgment, fine procedures, team communication, and postoperative responsibility; interest assessments can only serve as exploration clues.

The U.S. 2025 median annual wage for this occupation is 358,550 U.S. dollars; the Chinese mainland lacks a nationwide wage distribution for the same occupational scope and cannot be directly converted.

During outpatient visits and consultations, verify history, medication allergies, physical signs, and imaging, identify fractures, joint, and spinal problems, and decide whether further examination or surgery is needed.
Planning must consider expected benefit, anesthesia and surgical risk, alternatives, and patient preferences; handle and record key decisions within the organization's authorization.

Before surgery, verify the patient, site, procedure, team, and aseptic conditions; during surgery, collaborate with anesthesia and nursing teams; after surgery, manage complications and rehabilitation follow-up.

This page describes the U.S. 29-1242 non-pediatric orthopedic surgeons, including the diagnosis, treatment, and surgery of musculoskeletal disease, and does not exclude their non-surgical treatment; pediatric orthopedics, anesthesia, nursing, and rehabilitation physicians each have independent occupations and licensing scopes and do not grant authority to one another.

Orthopedic surgeons can participate in different directions such as trauma, joint replacement, spine, sports medicine, and hand and foot; the specific procedures depend on training, ability, and hospital authorization.

The work often includes ward rounds, operating rooms, outpatient clinics, emergency consultations, and interdisciplinary discussions; working hours and responsibility vary with position and organization.

Clinical communication, case discussions, and team handover can be observed through formal shadowing; diagnosis, treatment, and surgery for real patients must be undertaken by qualified and authorized personnel.

Orthopedic surgery and rehabilitation medicine both focus on functional recovery, but the former may perform surgery within authorization while the latter focuses on non-surgical rehabilitation assessment and training.

Both orthopedic surgeons and neurosurgeons may handle spinal problems; their respective diagnostic and treatment scopes and procedures are determined by training, organizational division of labor, and authorization.
General surgery and orthopedic surgery both require perioperative ability; orthopedics focuses on the bone, joint, muscle, ligament, and tendon systems.
Rehabilitation medicine physicians focus on non-surgical functional assessment and rehabilitation plans; orthopedic surgeons may perform orthopedic surgery within organizational authorization.

If you are more interested in non-surgical functional recovery and long-term rehabilitation, you can learn about rehabilitation medicine; transferring to another specialty still requires completing the corresponding training and practice verification.
Imaging and medical record materials
Decision support: models can prompt possible diagnoses or preoperative risks, but cannot independently decide surgical indications, procedure, or informed consent.

Preoperative planning: three-dimensional reconstruction, navigation, and template tools can assist with positioning and simulation; real anatomy, intraoperative changes, and instrument fitting are verified by the surgical team.

Surgical robots and navigation: positioning assistance is a candidate use, and accuracy or efficacy improvement cannot be asserted based on the occupational description; specific devices require separate verification of clinical validation, applicable conditions, training, and organizational procedures, and physicians retain control and handling responsibility.
Perioperative monitoring: anomaly alerts can assist in identifying risks; clinical personnel are responsible for interpreting signals, handling them, and recording escalation.
Patient communication: automatic drafts can help explain preoperative preparation and rehabilitation matters; the team must verify individual applicability and privacy boundaries.

Adoption judgment: technology availability, clinical validation, hospital procurement, and job changes are different questions, and the existing materials cannot derive this occupation's automation proportion.
Ability preparation: learn imaging interpretation, data quality, device limitations, bias, and failure response, while strengthening surgical technique and cross-specialty communication.

Insufficient evidence: nationwide medians, percentiles, and starting pay for Chinese non-pediatric orthopedic surgeons were not obtained. In 2025, pre-tax annual averages for health and social work were 146,266 yuan for urban non-private and 75,631 yuan for private, which is only a broad medical institution employer industry, includes other clinical and social work positions and is not orthopedic wages or an individual range; excludes self-employed individuals and freelancers and owner-operated clinic profits, and device manufacturing and pure research employers require separate verification.
When comparing position compensation, verify region, hospital tier, department, title, surgical authorization, on-call duty, performance, and statistical period.
NBS industry average wages cannot be treated as orthopedic surgeons' starting pay, personal take-home income, or occupational median.
To judge a specific position, keep the current job posting and compensation structure and verify whether it is in fact an orthopedic surgeon position.
The 2025 median annual wage cited by the U.S. O*NET 29-1242.00 is 358,550 U.S. dollars/year, describing only U.S. precise occupational statistics.
That median is not starting pay, monthly pay, a personal income promise, or Chinese income; region, hospital, employment form, and seniority all affect offers.

The 2025 official national annual wages at P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 are 84,170/180,610/358,550/530,700/659,290 U.S. dollars; the same precise 29-1242 occupation, not representing starting pay or seniority levels.

The Chinese mainland path first verifies medical education, physician qualification, and practice registration, then orthopedic specialty training and the organization's surgical grading authorization.

The U.S. path usually includes a medical degree, licensure, and orthopedic residency training; the O*NET Job Zone 5 only indicates the preparation level and does not constitute a license. Problem statement: fictional U01 history records the left knee, the imaging label records the right knee, and the request records the left knee; V01 the three sites agree, but the allergy field reads not verified, the team review is blank, and release is planned per the schedule. Paper rule: identifiers and site must agree, documents must be complete, and review must be explicit; unknown does not equal negative, and scheduling does not equal approval. List the pending verification points for both cases, and do not decide procedure or treatment.
Early on, foundations can be built through formal education, anatomy and imaging study, and supervised case discussions; real patients cannot be independently diagnosed and treated.

During residency, assessment, perioperative care, and surgical skills are accumulated under senior physician supervision and organizational rules. Reference: U01 keeps each original value, marks the left/right contradiction, and hands it to the original record's responsible person for verification, without changing the side; for V01, list the unverified allergy and blank review as unresolved and do not mark it releasable based on the schedule. The work submits a two-line material verification table and a simulated anomaly transfer draft, stating the missing items, original values, person to verify, and correction records; it is not clinical diagnosis or surgical permission.

Becoming an independent orthopedic surgeon still requires meeting the local practice registration, position appointment, technical ability, and organizational surgical grading management requirements.
Further specialization in trauma, joints, spine, or sports medicine requires verifying the specific training, case experience, and procedure authorization.
When job hunting, verify with the organization the procedures that can be performed, mentoring, emergency on-call duty, complication rescue support, and performance basis.

Continuous development verifies ability through quality data, case discussions, complication review, and continuing education, and the number of certificates cannot replace results. Seven days: Day 1 copy the U/V inputs and paper rules; Days 2—3 list the two-line table for laterality, allergy, and review status; Days 4—5 write the pending-verification transfer draft that keeps the original values; Days 6—7 submit the table, draft, and simulated review feedback and correction records. Both cases remain unresolved until verified, no real cases are used, and the side is not changed, nor are procedures, drugs, or tests selected.
